name: Energia
dispatch: Energia was the rocket that redeemed the N1 — the super-heavy launcher the Soviet Union finally got right. Where the N1 exploded on all four attempts, Energia worked, lifting the Polyus payload in 1987 and the Buran orbiter in 1988. Crucially, it was a launcher in its own right, not a shuttle stack: because Buran had no main engines, Energia did the whole job of reaching orbit and could just as well have lifted other heavy payloads with no orbiter at all. It was the most powerful rocket the Soviet Union ever flew successfully — and, like Buran, it was cancelled for want of anything left to launch.
description: The only Soviet super-heavy launcher to fly successfully. Designed to carry the Buran orbiter or stand-alone payloads up to 100 t to LEO. Two flights: Polyus payload test (1987) and Buran orbiter (1988), both successful. Program shelved at the end of the Cold War.
